A workflow is a YAML file that declares a graph of nodes. Each node runs an agent, a command file, a shell or script step, a loop, a pause, or another workflow. Nodes declare what they depend on; nodes without a dependency between them run in parallel.

description: Investigate an issue, then fix it in a fresh session

  - id: investigate
    command: investigate-issue

  - id: implement
    command: implement-issue
    depends_on: [investigate]
    context: fresh

'loop_group.interactive' with 'gate_message' and '$LOOP_USER_INPUT' is deprecated. Write a 'loop_group' whose body ends in a 'wait: attention' node instead; the next iteration reads '$LOOP_PREV.<id>.output.text', and 'until_bash' checks the answer at '$<id>.output'.

'approval:' is deprecated. Write 'wait: { attention: <message>, form: approval }' instead; the next node reads '$<id>.output.decision' and '$<id>.output.text'. A legacy reject cancels the run, while an attention wait continues with decision 'reject', so add a 'cancel:' node with when: "$<id>.output.decision == 'reject'" where rejecting should end the run.
'approval.decisions' is deprecated. Write 'wait: { attention: <message>, form: select, options: <the same decisions> }' instead; the output is the same {decision, text}.
'approval.capture_response' is deprecated. An attention wait always records the answer; the next node reads '$<id>.output.text'.

'approval.on_reject' and '$REJECTION_REASON' are deprecated. Write 'wait: { attention: <message>, form: approval }' followed by a rework node with when: "$<id>.output.decision == 'reject'" that reads '$<id>.output.text'. To repeat the rework, write a 'loop_group' whose body ends in the wait; the rework node comes first and reads '$LOOP_PREV.<id>.output.text'.
